sensors.guide: The solution must build before the turn ends.
Run dotnet test before claiming done; fix the code, never the tests.
dotnet format must report no changes; do not suppress analyzers without a reason.
Respect the layer rules in the architecture tests.
Reuse existing code instead of copying it; the duplicated share may not grow past its baseline.

sensors.cmd: if semgrep --version >/dev/null 2>&1; then semgrep scan --config p/default --error --metrics=off --disable-version-check --quiet {changed}; s=$?; [ $s -le 1 ] || [ -n "$CI" ] && exit $s; echo "sast: Semgrep could not scan here (exit $s: offline, or the rules did not load), so CI scans this change"; elif [ -n "$CI" ]; then echo 'sast: Semgrep does not run in CI (pipx install semgrep)'; exit 1; else echo 'sast: Semgrep does not run here (missing or broken), so CI scans this change (pipx install semgrep to scan locally)'; fi
sensors.guide: Semgrep scans the source files this change touches for security bugs (injection, unsafe input, secrets, weak crypto); fix the code rather than silencing the rule.
Do not add packages with known vulnerabilities.

sensors.cmd: dotnet stryker --version >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo 'mutation-diff: Stryker.NET is not installed: dotnet tool install -g dotnet-stryker, or the person waives mutation-diff'; exit 1; }; rm -rf StrykerOutput; { set -f; dotnet stryker $(for f in {changed:cs}; do printf -- '-m **/%s ' "$f"; done) --reporter json || true; set +f; } >&2; node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning "$RIG_SDLC" mutscore --tool stryker-net --report "$(ls -t StrykerOutput/*/reports/mutation-report.json 2>/dev/null | head -1)" --lines {changed-lines:cs}; s=$?; rm -rf StrykerOutput; exit $s
sensors.guide: Every line this change adds is pinned by a test: the mutation score on the changed lines must reach mutation.minScore; a survivor names a line and a change no test noticed, and goes back to the test writer.
Tests must assert behaviour so that changing the code makes them fail.
